question:
Let $p(x),q(x)$ be distinct polynomials with real coefficients such that the sum of the coefficients of each of the polynomials equals $s$. If $(p(x))^3-(q(x))^3=p(x^3)-q(x^3)$, then prove the following:

1. $p(x)-q(x)=(x-1)^a r(x)$ for some integer $a\ge1$ and a polynomial $r(x)$ with $r(1)\ne0$.

2. $s^2=3^{a-1}$ where $a$ is as given in (a).

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
